LESSON: WRITING 12.5.1 THE WRITING PROCESS: DIALOGUES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.5: Writing 12.5.1 The Writing Process: Dialogues
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 12.5.1 The Writing Process: Dialogues, part of Strand 12 in Grade 7 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What should we consider before writing a dialogue?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online and offline for an example of a dialogue,

2. dramatise the identified dialogue,

3. discuss the format of the dialogue they have identified,

4. fill in missing words in a set dialogue on traditional fashion, individually,

5. discuss the correctness of the words they have used,

6. create a rough draft of a short dialogue using the format they have identified individually,

7. edit each other’s dialogue to check for repetition, clarity, grammar, spelling and punctuation errors, in pairs,

8. revise the dialogue individually,

9. publish the final product for assessment, share the samples of well written dialogues with others in class.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online and offline for an example of a dialogue,
2. dramatise the identified dialogue,
3. discuss the format of the dialogue they have identified,
4. fill in missing words in a set dialogue on traditional fashion, individually,
5. discuss the correctness of the words they have used,
6. create a rough draft of a short dialogue using the format they have identified individually,
7. edit each other’s dialogue to check for repetition, clarity, grammar, spelling and punctuation errors, in pairs,
8. revise the dialogue individually,
9. publish the final product for assessment, share the samples of well written dialogues with others in class.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 12.5.1 The Writing Process: Dialogues together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Collaboration: It is enhanced when the learner observes the rules of engagement as they discuss the format of

the dialogue identified in groups.

Values:
• Responsibility is enhanced when the learner takes up the task of editing and assessing their peers’ dialogues.

• Unity is achieved as learners work together to generate ideas for writing tasks.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Effective communication is enhanced as learners communicate effectively through writing.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates the skill of writing dialogues to similar writing in Kiswahili.
